Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{\frac{1}{8}}{\sqrt{1 - 64 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "596c3e80-0a77-5c0b-9dd5-ac5db525f1a6" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=8 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{1}{8}}{\sqrt{1 - 64 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{8}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(8 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{8}(\frac{1}{8})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{64}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{64}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(8 x \right)}}{64}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "596c3e80-0a77-5c0b-9dd5-ac5db525f1a6" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "596c3e80-0a77-5c0b-9dd5-ac5db525f1a6" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{1 - 3 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "86099405-77c6-5190-8a2a-9987ead0ebf9" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=\sqrt{3} x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\sqrt{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{\sqrt{1 - 3 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 4\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\sqrt{3} x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 4(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{3}+C \\  &= \frac{4 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\sqrt{3} x \right)}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "86099405-77c6-5190-8a2a-9987ead0ebf9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "86099405-77c6-5190-8a2a-9987ead0ebf9" :question/answer-fields $$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\sqrt{10} x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 1(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{10})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10}}{10}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{10}+C \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{10} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\sqrt{10} x \right)}}{10}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "eb6f8ce4-1f1e-518a-95af-5865fb0347a5" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "eb6f8ce4-1f1e-518a-95af-5865fb0347a5" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{\frac{8}{5}}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "b827135e-0cd3-5561-ac5d-10676a4c5f9e" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{4(1-(\frac{1}{4})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(2)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{8}{5}}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{2})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(2)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "b827135e-0cd3-5561-ac5d-10676a4c5f9e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "b827135e-0cd3-5561-ac5d-10676a4c5f9e" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{3}{4}}{\sqrt{81 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{9})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{12}(9)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{4}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C \\  &= \frac{3 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{9} \right)}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "e801a538-fddf-55dd-bfcb-170ff82d56d9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "e801a538-fddf-55dd-bfcb-170ff82d56d9" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{\frac{6}{5}}{\sqrt{49 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "5d1a2e08-17a0-5035-83a4-af508eb0495e" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{49 - 2 x^{2}}=\sqrt{49(1-(\frac{2}{49})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{6}{5}}{\sqrt{49 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{35}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{35}(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "5d1a2e08-17a0-5035-83a4-af508eb0495e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "5d1a2e08-17a0-5035-83a4-af508eb0495e" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{25 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "1df3778e-4e82-53f7-a9f2-51a498e80f46" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{25 - 10 x^{2}}=\sqrt{25(1-(\frac{2}{5})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{5}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{\sqrt{25 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{5})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{5} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "1df3778e-4e82-53f7-a9f2-51a498e80f46" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "1df3778e-4e82-53f7-a9f2-51a498e80f46" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}=\sqrt{4(1-(\frac{1}{2})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{2}+C \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2} \right)}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{\frac{9}{5}}{\sqrt{36 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x

$$
\sqrt{36 - 7 x^{2}}=\sqrt{36(1-(\frac{7}{36})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{6 \sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{9}{5}}{\sqrt{36 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{10}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{10}(\frac{6 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{35}+C \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6} \right)}}{35}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "a7ba47cf-596e-5b89-8f83-7c1f409bdcdd" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "a7ba47cf-596e-5b89-8f83-7c1f409bdcdd" :question/answer-fields $$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{9}{\sqrt{9 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{3})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3(\frac{3 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{7}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{7}+C \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{3} \right)}}{7}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "c3725f6e-6465-5347-b4c3-9fbe02106733" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "c3725f6e-6465-5347-b4c3-9fbe02106733" :question/answer-fields $$"] [:db/add "aeb4b559-27b4-5499-b515-6939cb760420" :question/worked-solution "Use the linear substitution $u=8 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=8,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{8})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 64 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(8 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3(\frac{1}{8})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{8}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{8}+C \\  &= \frac{3 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(8 x \right)}}{8}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "aeb4b559-27b4-5499-b515-6939cb760420" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "aeb4b559-27b4-5499-b515-6939cb760420" :question/answer-fields $$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(2)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{8}{5}}{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{2})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(2)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{2} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "b827135e-0cd3-5561-ac5d-10676a4c5f9e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "b827135e-0cd3-5561-ac5d-10676a4c5f9e" :question/answer-fields $$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{9}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{9},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(9)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{81 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{9})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{9}(9)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 1\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{9} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "fbda043b-7d01-51c0-ac35-cea779e23de9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "fbda043b-7d01-51c0-ac35-cea779e23de9" :question/answer-fields $$

$$"] [:db/add "9c2f398a-4d2e-5089-b8b8-70c8313ce43a" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{9(1-(\frac{1}{9})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(3)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{8}{5}}{\sqrt{9 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{8}{15}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{3})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{8}{15}(3)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{8 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{3} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "9c2f398a-4d2e-5089-b8b8-70c8313ce43a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "9c2f398a-4d2e-5089-b8b8-70c8313ce43a" :question/answer-fields $$
\sqrt{81 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{81(1-(\frac{1}{81})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{9}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{9},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(9)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{3}{4}}{\sqrt{81 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{12}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{9})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{12}(9)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3}{4}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{4}+C \\  &= \frac{3 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{9} \right)}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "e801a538-fddf-55dd-bfcb-170ff82d56d9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "e801a538-fddf-55dd-bfcb-170ff82d56d9" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{4}{\sqrt{36 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "a57f0d65-3f7b-5093-8b5d-c66248b0abe5" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{36 - 2 x^{2}}=\sqrt{36(1-(\frac{1}{18})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(3 \sqrt{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{\sqrt{36 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{3}(3 \sqrt{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2 \sqrt{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6} \right)}+C\end{aligned}

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{\frac{6}{5}}{\sqrt{49 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "5d1a2e08-17a0-5035-83a4-af508eb0495e" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{49 - 2 x^{2}}=\sqrt{49(1-(\frac{2}{49})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{7},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{6}{5}}{\sqrt{49 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{35}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{6}{35}(\frac{7 \sqrt{2}}{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{3 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{7} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "5d1a2e08-17a0-5035-83a4-af508eb0495e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "5d1a2e08-17a0-5035-83a4-af508eb0495e" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{\sqrt{25 - 10 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{5})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{4}{5}(\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10}}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{10} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{10} x}{5} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}

Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}=\sqrt{4(1-(\frac{1}{2})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{2}+C \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2} \right)}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/answer-fields Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{\frac{9}{5}}{\sqrt{36 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "a7ba47cf-596e-5b89-8f83-7c1f409bdcdd" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{36 - 7 x^{2}}=\sqrt{36(1-(\frac{7}{36})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{6 \sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{9}{5}}{\sqrt{36 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{10}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{3}{10}(\frac{6 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{35}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{35}+C \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{6} \right)}}{35}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "a7ba47cf-596e-5b89-8f83-7c1f409bdcdd" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "a7ba47cf-596e-5b89-8f83-7c1f409bdcdd" :question/answer-fields $$
\int \frac{9}{\sqrt{9 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$"] [:db/add "c3725f6e-6465-5347-b4c3-9fbe02106733" :question/worked-solution "First factor the constant in the denominator:

$$
\sqrt{9 - 7 x^{2}}=\sqrt{9(1-(\frac{7}{9})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{3}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{3 \sqrt{7}}{7})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{9}{\sqrt{9 - 7 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{3})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= 3(\frac{3 \sqrt{7}}{7})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7}}{7}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{7}+C \\  &= \frac{9 \sqrt{7} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{7} x}{3} \right)}}{7}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "c3725f6e-6465-5347-b4c3-9fbe02106733" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "c3725f6e-6465-5347-b4c3-9fbe02106733" :question/answer-fields $$
\sqrt{9 - 3 x^{2}}=\sqrt{9(1-(\frac{1}{3})x^{2})}
$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{3})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{6}{5}}{\sqrt{9 - 3 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{3})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{5}(\sqrt{3})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{5}+C \\  &= \frac{2 \sqrt{3} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} x}{3} \right)}}{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] [:db/add "95936323-2406-5bb2-859c-74d73dc5a714" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "95936323-2406-5bb2-859c-74d73dc5a714" :question/answer-fields $$
\sqrt{36 - x^{2}}=\sqrt{36(1-(\frac{1}{36})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{x}{6}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(6)\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{2}{\sqrt{36 - x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{3}(6)\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 2 \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{x}{6} \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] ["cc91b79d-2e80-5826-ab2d-40a1036ba80b" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["cc91b79d-2e80-5826-ab2d-40a1036ba80b" :question/answer-fields "e75c4dd2-8d4a-5406-8e98-9ad1ab0f5124"] $$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(3 \sqrt{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{4}{\sqrt{36 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{2}{3}(3 \sqrt{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2 \sqrt{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= 2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C \\  &= 2 \sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{6} \right)}+C\end{aligned}

$$
\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}=\sqrt{4(1-(\frac{1}{2})x^{2})}
$$

Use the linear substitution $u=\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{2})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - 2 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{2})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{2}+C \\  &= \frac{\sqrt{2} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} x}{2} \right)}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$"] ["c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["c401b599-aeb3-532e-ad3b-4af24ac3d788" :question/answer-fields "d8e1c793-b298-5ef3-8a3d-aeb9c648f8f7"]
